name: A Tale of Valour: Major Somnath Sharma and the Battle of Badgam

scenes.animation: Dawn over snowy Kashmir hills. A young officer with his left arm in a white plaster cast checks a map with his soldiers. Zippy salutes, then stares at the cast.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Wait, he has a broken arm! Shouldn't he be resting in hospital?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He refused. Meet Major Somnath Sharma, the hero of A Tale of Valour.

scenes.animation: A simple animated map of Jammu and Kashmir. Dates appear on a timeline: 'October 1947: Kashmir accedes to India', then 'Infiltrators advance towards Srinagar'. A small airfield icon near Srinagar starts blinking red.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 1947, soon after Independence, armed infiltrators attacked Kashmir. After Kashmir acceded to India in October, Indian troops were flown in to defend it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Srinagar airfield was vital. If it fell, no more troops could land.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Major Sharma's arm was in plaster, but he insisted on going with his company of the 4 Kumaon Battalion.

scenes.animation: The timeline stops at '3 November 1947 — Badgam'. On one side, a small group labelled '90 soldiers'; on the other, a huge crowd labelled 'about 500'. A counter shows '7 to 1'. Mortar flashes light up the hills.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: On 3 November 1947, near the village of Badgam, about ninety Indian soldiers faced nearly five hundred attackers.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: That's about seven against one! How do you even fight that?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: With courage. Major Sharma ran from trench to trench, handing out ammunition and cheering his men on, even with one arm.

scenes.animation: A radio crackles; the major speaks into it. His words appear in bold on screen: 'I shall not withdraw an inch but will fight to the last man.' Then a bright flash, and the scene fades to a quiet, respectful silhouette against the dawn sky.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In his last message he said he would not withdraw an inch, but would fight to the last man.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Soon after, a mortar shell killed him. His company held on for hours, until more Indian troops arrived. Srinagar was saved.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Major Somnath Sharma became the first person to receive the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest award for bravery in war.

scenes.animation: A theme wall with four glowing badges: 'Courage', 'Duty', 'Leadership', 'Sacrifice'. Word cards slide in: 'hold their ground', 'fight to the last man', 'battalion, regiment, squadron, fleet'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: courage, duty and selfless leadership. He led from the front and put his country before himself.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Learn the idioms: to hold one's ground means not to retreat. And the collective nouns: a battalion of soldiers, a squadron of aircraft, a fleet of ships.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. Why is Major Sharma called a true leader?' Answer points build: 'Fought despite plaster', 'Moved among his men', 'Refused to retreat', 'Inspired his company'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker flashes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: why is Major Somnath Sharma remembered as a true leader?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: mention his injured arm, how he moved among his soldiers under fire, his refusal to retreat, and how he inspired his men.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: write the date and place correctly. Badgam, 3 November 1947. Small facts earn easy marks.

scenes.animation: Recap board framed like a medal ribbon: '1. 1947: defending the Srinagar airfield', '2. Badgam: about 90 against 500', '3. First Param Vir Chakra'. Zippy stands straight and salutes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: in 1947, Major Sharma's company had to protect the Srinagar airfield.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: at Badgam, about ninety soldiers held off nearly five hundred attackers.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: he gave his life and received the first Param Vir Chakra.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Not one inch. I'm going to remember that line forever.

name: Somebody's Mother by Mary Dow Brine

scenes.animation: A snowy, slushy city street. Crowds rush past an old woman in a grey shawl standing at the kerb. Zippy tries to wave at people, but everyone walks past her without looking.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Why is nobody stopping? She clearly needs help crossing!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That is exactly the question in the poem Somebody's Mother by Mary Dow Brine.

scenes.animation: Close-up of the old woman: bent, trembling, looking at the busy, slippery road with fear. A pack of noisy schoolboys runs by, laughing and throwing snowballs, not noticing her.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The woman is old, poor and weak. The street is wet and slippery with snow, and she is afraid to cross alone.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: People hurry past. Even a group of happy schoolboys rushes by without noticing her.

scenes.animation: One boy stops, turns back and gently offers his arm. He guides her step by step across the road while carts pass. His friends watch, puzzled. A speech bubble appears as he rejoins them.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then one boy stops. He takes her arm and guides her safely across.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When he returns, he tells his friends why. She is somebody's mother. If his own mother were old and poor and far away, he would hope someone would help her too.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Oh. That's a really good reason.

scenes.animation: Evening in a tiny, warm room. The old woman kneels and prays, a soft golden glow around her. Caption: 'God, be kind to the noble boy'. The title words 'somebody's mother' and 'somebody's son' glow side by side.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That night, the old woman prays for the kind boy, who is somebody's son and somebody's pride.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Notice the balance. She is somebody's mother. He is somebody's son. Kindness links strangers like family.

scenes.animation: A devices board: 'Narrative poem: tells a story', 'Imagery: snow, slippery street, bent figure', 'Contrast: rushing crowd vs the one kind boy', 'Repetition of somebody'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: This is a narrative poem. It tells a story with a beginning, middle and end.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The poet uses imagery of the cold, wet street, and a strong contrast between the uncaring crowd and the one kind boy.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: kindness, empathy and respect for the elderly.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. Why did the boy help the old woman?' Answer arrows link 'empathy' to a picture of the boy's own mother at home. An 'Exam Tip' sticker glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: why did the boy help the old woman?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: he imagined his own mother in her place. That empathy made him act, while others passed by.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: link the answer to the title. The title reminds us every old person is somebody's mother.

scenes.animation: Recap board on a snowy background: '1. An old woman fears the slippery street', '2. One boy helps her, thinking of his mother', '3. Theme: empathy for the elderly'. Zippy offers his tiny spark-hand to a passing grandmother.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: an old woman stands afraid on a snowy, busy street.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: one boy helps her, because she is somebody's mother.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the poem teaches empathy and respect for the elderly.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Auntie, may I help you cross? Don't worry, I'm very bright.

name: Verghese Kurien - I Too Had a Dream

scenes.animation: A teenager scrolls a phone, sending quick emojis. Then a paper envelope drifts in and lands on his desk. Zippy peeks at it in disbelief.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: A handwritten letter? Who does that anymore?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Dr Verghese Kurien did. This chapter is his letter to his grandson, sharing the dream that shaped his life.

scenes.animation: An elderly man with white hair writes at a desk. The letter's first lines glow. A split screen shows quick chat messages vanishing, while the letter is folded into a box of keepsakes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Kurien begins by saying letters matter. Quick messages are soon forgotten, but a letter can be kept and read again for years.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So he writes down his life story for his grandson, Siddharth.

scenes.animation: Three glowing doors appear before a young Kurien: 'Comfortable job', 'Career elsewhere', 'Settle abroad'. He walks past them to a dusty village road with a sign: 'Anand, Gujarat'. Cows and farmers with milk cans wave.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: As a young engineer, Kurien had many comfortable options, including a life abroad.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Instead he chose to work with dairy farmers in Anand, a small town in Gujarat, where life was hard.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: He picked the dusty road on purpose? That's brave.

scenes.animation: Farmers pour milk into one big shared can labelled 'Cooperative'. The can grows and grows; a map of India fills with white. A woman, his wife, stands beside Kurien, smiling through the tough village years.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He helped the farmers work together in a cooperative, so the profit reached the people who produced the milk.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He tells his grandson that his wife supported him through the difficult early years. His success was teamwork.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Fun fact: Kurien is often called the Father of the White Revolution in India.

scenes.animation: A values board with four badges: 'Honesty', 'Hard work', 'Service', 'Teamwork'. Grammar cards pop up: 'its / it's', 'their / they're', 'your / you're', and a long dash '—' marked 'em dash'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: a meaningful life is one spent serving others, with honesty and hard work.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The chapter also practises homophones like its and it's, and their and they're. It's means it is. Its shows possession.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. What values does Kurien want his grandson to learn?' Answer points build: 'Service over comfort', 'Honesty', 'Teamwork'. A 'Writing Tip' sticker appears beside a letter format outline.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: what values does Kurien want to pass on to his grandson?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: give his choice of service over comfort as an example, then name honesty, hard work and teamwork.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: this is an informal letter. If asked to reply to it, use a warm tone, a date, and a friendly closing.

scenes.animation: Recap board shaped like a letter: '1. Letters last longer than quick messages', '2. Kurien chose to serve farmers in Anand', '3. Service, honesty, teamwork'. Zippy scribbles his first letter to Neo.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Kurien writes to his grandson because letters last.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: he gave up comfort to serve dairy farmers in Anand.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: his message is service, honesty and teamwork.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Dear Neo, please write back. With emojis, if possible.
